name: Nightcrawler
bio: Teleporting, devoutly Catholic circus acrobat whose demonic appearance belies the team's gentlest temperament. The son of Mystique; best friend of Wolverine; the character most often used to argue that the X-Men's faith in people is justified.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Best friends; the devil and the saint
relationships.summary: The franchise's most consistently written male friendship. Kurt is the one person Logan does not perform for; Kurt's death in X-Force vol. 3 #26 (2010) broke Logan, and his return on Krakoa restored the pairing.

events.note: Early baseball-game issue establishing the team's off-duty bonds.
Nightcrawler dies saving Hope Summers; Logan carries the grief for years.

continuity.name: Earth-616

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: From fear to family
relationships.summary: Kitty initially recoiled from Kurt's appearance; Claremont used her growing affection for him as the story of the reader learning to see past surfaces. They are close for the rest of the run.

events.note: Kitty is frightened by Nightcrawler on first meeting.
Christmas issue: Kitty alone at the mansion, Kurt among those she now counts as family.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: 90s / Blue-Gold
era.description: Jim Lee's X-Men relaunch through the Onslaught and Apocalypse: The Twelve era. Rogue and Gambit, the Blue and Gold teams, Age of Apocalypse.

relationships.label: Mother who abandoned him
relationships.summary: Hinted at since Uncanny X-Men #142 (1981) and confirmed in 1994: Mystique bore Kurt and, fleeing a mob, let him fall into a river. The relationship is about whether he can forgive her and whether she wants him to. Krakoa, where she sat on the Quiet Council while he served as its moral voice, kept the question open.

events.note: Mystique hints she knows Nightcrawler's parentage.
Mystique confirms she is Kurt's mother.
'The Draco' names Azazel as his father.
